description: String-mode coupling (the deck rows), their persistent mute masks, and the output sound-channel tables.

domains.title: Deck feed-in (string -> mode)
domains.write: param.set {parameter: feedin, key_no, values} (values = {pitch: [num_modes]}); to silence modes use param.mute_modes (mask, don't zero)
domains.key_space: piano PITCH (not a mode; feedin/3 addresses pitch 3, a mode index is 416); output pitches 128+ are rejected 416
domains.shape: [num_modes] row per pitch, indexed by mode
domains.stored_vs_effective: Raw row stored; effective = raw x feedin_mask at pack time. Values are a per-mode normalised spatial coupling in 0..1 (1 = the mode's spatial maximum over all bridge positions); raw un-normalised magnitudes (~1e-4) give near-silent output. On a flat-tier preset one value is written to all flat columns of an edited row (/health mode_layout). No Layer B level class.

domains.title: Deck feedback (mode -> string) and strings-axis output rows
domains.read: param.get {parameter: feedback, key_no} (key_no 'output' or 'from128to<127+n>' for the output rows)
domains.write: param.set {parameter: feedback, key_no, values}; strings-axis channel rows: param.set {parameter: feedback, key_no: 128+ch}; mutes: param.mute_modes / param.mute_channels
domains.key_space: piano pitch, AND the output pitches 128..127+num_output_channels (the only raw domain that may address them; REST_API also documents the alias parameter name 'output' for these rows)
domains.shape: [num_modes] row per pitch, indexed by mode
domains.stored_vs_effective: Raw row stored; effective = raw x feedback_mask at pack time. Feedback equals feedin by reciprocity for piano pitches; an output pitch's row carries the mode shape at that receiver and, in strings listen mode (listen_to_modes=0), IS the channel's output path. The runtime deck feedback coefficient scales the piano-pitch rows only (output rows >= 128 stay x1). Whether piano-pitch feedback rows are independently effective under the single-deck build is a doc conflict (see _index.json).

domains.title: Output-pitch feedback rows (documented alias)
domains.read: param.get {parameter: feedback, key_no: output} (use the canonical name; the 'output' parameter name is a documented alias that was not confirmed in the GET route's parameter list)
domains.shape: [num_modes] row per output pitch, indexed by mode
domains.stored_vs_effective: Same rows as feedback at 128+ (see feedback): in strings listen mode (listen_to_modes=0) they are the per-channel output path.

domains.title: Feed-in mute mask
domains.write: param.mute_modes {modes, pitches?, side: feedin|both, action}; or param.set {parameter: feedin_mask, key_no, values}
domains.key_space: same pitch key space as feedin (piano pitches)
domains.stored_vs_effective: The mask itself is stored and persistent; it is applied as a pure multiply at pack time (deck[m] x deck_mask[m]); the raw feedin row is untouched, so unmute restores it bit-exactly.

envelope.note: mute / solo / unmute only switch existing rows on or off (no magnitude); an unmute is covered by the post-write level watch. A raw param.set of a mask row asks.

domains.title: Feedback mute mask (incl. strings-axis channel mute)
domains.write: param.mute_modes {side: feedback|both} for piano pitches; param.mute_channels for output channels when listen_to_modes=0 (row 128+ch); or param.set {parameter: feedback_mask, key_no, values}
domains.key_space: same pitch key space as feedback, including the output pitches 128+
domains.stored_vs_effective: Persistent mask, applied as a multiply at pack time; the raw feedback row is untouched. In strings listen mode the row of output pitch 128+ch is the mask that mutes output channel ch.

envelope.note: mute / solo / unmute only switch existing rows on or off (no magnitude); an unmute is covered by the post-write level watch. A raw param.set of a mask row asks.

domains.title: Modes-axis sound-channel coupling
domains.read: param.get {parameter: sound_channel, key_no} (the payload adds _meta {num_channels, mode_channel_index})
domains.shape: [num_channels] row per pitch, indexed by output channel
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored for every pitch 0..139; effective ONLY in modes listen mode (listen_to_modes=1), piano-pitch rows 0..127, injected into the feedin slots at mode_channel_index. Inert in strings mode (measured: x50 on p60 -> no level change). Units UNKNOWN in the docs. No Layer B level class.

domains.title: Modes-axis channel mute mask
domains.write: param.mute_channels {channels, action} when listen_to_modes=1 (column ch on every piano pitch); or param.set {parameter: sound_channel_mask, key_no, values}
domains.stored_vs_effective: Persistent mask; the modes-axis mute. Writing it on a listen_to_modes=0 preset is a silent no-op for the sound (measured).

envelope.note: mute / solo / unmute only switch existing rows on or off (no magnitude); an unmute is covered by the post-write level watch. A raw param.set of a mask row asks.

domains.title: Strings-mode per-channel gain table (FE-unused)
domains.read: param.get {parameter: string_sound_channel, key_no: output} (whole output table; a numeric output key such as 129 -> 416)
domains.write: param.set {parameter: string_sound_channel, key_no: output, values}; no FE writer
domains.key_space: stored for piano pitches by number, but effective rows are the output pitches 128..127+num_output_channels, addressed only via key_no 'output'
domains.shape: [num_channels] row per pitch, indexed by output channel
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored for every pitch 0..139; the kernel reads only the output-pitch rows 128+ in strings mode (listen_to_modes=0); piano-pitch rows are a NO-OP (POST succeeds, nothing audible). string_coefficients[128+ch][ch] is the gain on channel ch; off-diagonals mix channels. Old presets default to 40.0 per channel. A separate table from the one the Sound Channels editor edits (that writes feedback / feedback_mask at 128+ch). Units UNKNOWN.
